blocker.summary: The r436-r441 chain fully resolved the causal story with no residual contradiction, and r442 closed the last gap. sub_821D5F48 (the game's Xenos/renderer bootstrap, r441) has exactly two real exit points in its generated source: an early failure return (r3=0, label loc_821D6138, reached from 4 convergent sites) and a late success return (r3=1) sitting right after the store to 0x82935D98 that r441 found. r441's live breakpoint on that store never fired, and by elimination (only two exits exist, the write path is proven unreached, yet the function returns without crashing or hanging) sub_821D5F48 must take the early-failure return in this run -- it fails and never constructs the object. r442 corrected the 'must succeed' framing r440/r441 had used for the caller's response to that failure: sub_821F5B18 (called by sub_821D7DE0 when sub_821D5F48 returns 0) decompiles as a plain string-classifying/logging routine (strcmp-style loop against two reference strings, no abort/terminate instruction) -- and r440's own already-captured decompilation of sub_821D7DE0 shows no branch or return following that call at all; execution always continues regardless of success or failure. So the full chain is: sub_821D5F48 fails one of its internal checks in this offline environment (never writes 0x82935D98), sub_821D7DE0 logs that failure non-fatally and proceeds anyway, sub_821D6C20 runs unconditionally and crashes on the unguarded null dereference. This is no longer a 'why doesn't it abort' puzzle; the remaining open question is upstream -- which of sub_821D5F48's 4 failure-convergent checks (generated source lines 18900/19153/19629/20046) actually fails offline. Not resolved this cycle: correlating compiled x86 addresses back to those specific guest branch sites turned out to require more than simple textual search (the compiler reordered blocks, invalidating the position-based shortcut used successfully for the store instruction). Named for r443: pin down which of the 4 checks fails, likely by breaking on the callee each guards (their targets, unlike the branch sites themselves, are easy to locate live, as sub_820B1CD0/sub_82338300 already were). The native_vulkan_backend.cpp backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438) remains the other open, user-dependent thread.
